card: Prevents transactions sent via private broadcast from subsequently leaking origin identity through public broadcast paths. When transactions are re-submitted or rebroadcast via RPC, the wallet, or unbroadcast retry routines, PeerManager::InitiateTxBroadcastToAll would previously announce them to all connected peers. This change distinguishes requested broadcasts from standard peer relay, suppressing public announcements and clearing unbroadcast retry state if the transaction was previously tracked by private broadcast. Depends on #36477 to keep finished private broadcast records in memory.
evidence: Commit a100ddec89 details multiple pathways where private transactions are announced to all peers: submitpackage RPC, wallet periodic resend, GUI PSBT broadcast, and ReattemptInitialBroadcast.
PR description notes known historical leaks and referenced PRs addressing specific pathways (#36277, #36330, #36309).
problem: Transactions broadcast via private broadcast can inadvertently be leaked to public peers later if re-submitted or re-broadcast through other mechanisms such as the submitpackage RPC, periodic wallet rebroadcasts, GUI PSBT broadcast, or mempool unbroadcast reattempts.

risk.why: Mistakes in classifying broadcast reasons could suppress intended transaction relay or fail to prevent network privacy leaks.

scope_notes: The PR includes commits from unmerged prerequisite PR #36477, which preserves finished private broadcasts in memory so this guard can identify them.
summary: Adds a guard in PeerManager to block non-private broadcasts of transactions that were previously broadcast privately. It introduces a reason parameter (relay versus requested broadcast) to InitiateTxBroadcastToAll, suppressing requested broadcasts and clearing mempool unbroadcast tracking when a transaction matches known private broadcasts. Normal relay of transactions received from network peers remains unaffected.
